clue.text: Have influence on game: it should give greater opening for current moves

definitions.text: it should give greater opening for current moves

parts.note: to swing a vote or decision is to have influence on it
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone sways a match, then a cryptic aside about something opening wider for moves currently happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself cryptic: 'current' means the flow of water, and the bridge pivots to open a wider channel for passing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivoting bridge turns aside so vessels moving on the river's flow get a wider passage.

clue.text: Error about love upset miss having egotistical attitude

indicators.note: the error word goes around the love letter, as something placed about another

parts.note: a slip is a small error
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of miss are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A blunder over romance upsets a woman who is self-absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman, but 'upset' just rearranges its letters to SISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Solipsism is the philosophical view that only oneself exists, used loosely for extreme self-centredness.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine I think will get information

parts.note: IMO is texting shorthand for 'in my opinion', i.e. I think
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a Shakespeare heroine will be well informed.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information, as in 'get the gen on something'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is the heroine of Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: Heavy garment and other things wrapping one in a little bit

indicators.note: in says that wrapped group sits inside the little-bit word

parts.note: a groat was an old British coin of small value, so a tiny amount

indicators.note: wrapping says the other-things word goes around the one letter

parts.note: etc, et cetera, stands for other things
a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A heavy coat and other items bundled up in a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' makes EATC, which 'in' sets inside the little-bit word: a groat was an old British fourpenny coin, as in 'not worth a groat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, typically a military one.

clue.text: Source of colour initially absent in artificial silk

indicators.note: initially absent says the first letter of the colour source is missing

parts.note: a crayon is a stick children colour with

explanation.surface: Artificial silk lacks a colour source from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially absent' drops the C from CRAYON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a fibre made from cellulose, developed as a man-made substitute for silk.

clue.text: Unambitious in home improvements, sadly

indicators.note: in places the unambitious word inside the home improvements letters

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement done by the owner
small, as in small-minded or thinking small, means unambitious

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly does up their house, with regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismally and sadly are synonyms, both meaning in a gloomy, miserable way.

clue.text: Just one not accepted by European shrink

indicators.note: not accepted says the one letter is refused entry, so it is removed from the shrink word

parts.note: to quail is to shrink back in fear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fair-minded person is turned away by a European psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like the slang for a psychiatrist but is the verb, QUAIL; 'not accepted' removes the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and equal both mean fair, treating each side alike.

clue.text: Entirely welcoming a few in obsequious style

indicators.note: welcoming says the entirely word takes the few word in

parts.note: fully means entirely
some means a few

explanation.surface: Greeting a handful of guests with gushing flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome praise is excessive and flattering, so acting fulsomely is fawning, obsequious behaviour.

clue.text: Frenchman supporting sticker in Paris identifying actress's original name

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: Paris is in France, so a thing in Paris is France's
gum is a sticky substance
M is short for monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman holds up some glue in Paris, identifying a star's birth name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticker in Paris' reads as France's gum: FRANCES GUM; 'supporting' sets M beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances Gumm was the birth name of the film star Judy Garland.

clue.text: Second selection leads to row

parts.note: a cull is a selection, originally of animals picked out

explanation.surface: A second round of selection ends in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is the verb for propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to row a boat with oars, one in each hand.

clue.text: Group offering some light on airship

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above

parts.note: an LED, light-emitting diode, is a kind of light
a zeppelin is a German airship

explanation.surface: Someone shines a little light onto an airship.
explanation.definitionFit: Led Zeppelin were a British rock band, a group in the musical sense.

clue.text: Fruit mostly employed after I departed

indicators.note: departed says the letter I leaves the word
mostly says the employed word loses its last letter

parts.note: applied means put to use, employed

explanation.surface: Fruit mainly used up after someone left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' takes D off APPLIED, and with I 'departed' APPLIE becomes APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common fruit from orchard trees.

clue.text: Number attempted to dislodge king of octopoda?

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: to dislodge says the king letter is knocked out of the attempted word

parts.note: tackled means attempted, took on a task
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A number try to oust the ruler of the octopuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king of octopoda' looks like a phrase; 'king' is K for removal and 'of octopoda?' is the definition, the query marking a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopuses, the octopoda, have eight arms, so describing them as having tentacles fits.

clue.text: Smart greeting adopted by Conservatives

indicators.note: adopted by says the greeting is taken inside the Conservatives letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, doubled for the plural
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Tories take up a stylish way of saying hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, as smart does of dress.

clue.text: Catholic formerly touring valleys to get healthier

indicators.note: touring says the formerly word travels around the valleys word

parts.note: once means formerly
vales are valleys

explanation.surface: A Catholic once toured the valleys to regain health.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to recover after illness, gradually regaining strength.

clue.text: See a line I saw confirmed

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
to see someone can mean to go out with them romantically, i.e. dated them

explanation.surface: Someone asks you to look at a line they saw, now verified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the plain past of see, but here it means went out with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Validated means confirmed or proven to be sound.

clue.text: Cat identified from curious plain toes

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are put in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: A cat is recognised by its strange plain toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealpoint is a Siamese cat with dark brown points on a pale coat.

clue.text: I'd picked up novel serial from Victorian author

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone took up a serialised novel by a Victorian writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book but is the anagram signal for I'D plus SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli, the Victorian prime minister, also wrote novels such as Sybil.

clue.text: Whole exploit receiving tense thanks in high-level meeting

parts.note: a sum is a whole, a total

indicators.note: receiving says the exploit word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Taking full advantage while nervous gratitude flows at an important meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' gives MITTALK; TA is everyday British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a meeting of heads of government, the highest level of talks.

clue.text: Regular payments to secure Arab stringed instrument

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the payments letters close around the Arab letters

parts.note: HP, hire purchase, is the British term for buying on regular instalments
AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: Instalments are used to buy an Arab's stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: HP, hire purchase, is the British name for paying by instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp is a large instrument with strings plucked by the fingers.

clue.text: Gross expression of pain — not a happy bunny

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen
ouch is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A disgusting cry of pain comes from someone who is fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a habitual grumbler; 'not a happy bunny' is British slang for someone discontented.

clue.text: Single one brought in without blemish

indicators.note: brought in says the one letter is put inside the blemish word

parts.note: unmarred means without blemish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One person is introduced unblemished and unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: Single, as a marital status, means not having a spouse.

clue.text: Watery droplets filled with oxygen

indicators.note: filled with says the droplets word holds the oxygen letter

parts.note: mist is a cloud of tiny water droplets
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Wet droplets saturated with oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, damp with water.

clue.text: Spanish location in Iberia's foremost business area

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: biz is informal for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: A place in Spain at the heart of Iberia's leading commercial zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Balearics, famed for nightlife.

clue.text: Cancel legislation banning a revolt

indicators.note: banning says the letter a is barred from the cancelling word

parts.note: to repeal is to cancel a law

explanation.surface: Scrapping a law that forbade an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolt' looks like a noun, uprising, but is the verb meaning disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel and to revolt both mean to fill someone with disgust.

clue.text: Confusing arrangement surrounding one crop

indicators.note: surrounding says the arrangement word goes around the one letter

parts.note: a maze is a confusing arrangement of paths
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A baffling layout surrounds a single crop, like a maize maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is a cereal crop, also called corn.

clue.text: Stumbling into ruins — trespass?

indicators.note: stumbling suggests a confused fall, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trips into ruins they may not be allowed to enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is an unwelcome entry on to someone else's property or affairs.

clue.text: Various things trimmed slender ornate hatstand

indicators.note: trimmed says the slender word loses its final letter

parts.note: thin means slender

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately done up, so the letters are rearranged fancily

explanation.surface: Assorted items: a slim, decorated stand for hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts THIN to THI; 'ornate' rearranges HATSTAND into SANDTHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means miscellaneous items or topics, unspecified.
